topic: Chinese consumer acceptance of cultivated meat
claim_a: 59.3 percent of an urban online sample were very or extremely likely to buy clean meat (2018 fieldwork; NOV-28)
claim_b: In a 2020 discrete choice experiment in five cities, willingness to pay for cultivated meat was below farm-raised meat, and below plant-based meat (NOV-29)
position_taken: Prefer the choice experiment for pricing and demand design; treat the 59.3 percent as an upper bound on stated openness
notes: Different methods and years; the 2018 study also used the positive name 'purity meat'.

topic: Purchase intent for blended products in the 2025 Singapore blind test
claim_a: 22 percent would buy blended versus 16 percent plant-based (vegconomist, NOV-39)
claim_b: 58 percent would likely buy blended versus 38 percent plant-based and 95 percent conventional (Green Queen, NOV-38)
position_taken: Use the ratio (blends 1.4 to 1.5 times plant-based) and the gap to conventional meat, not either level
notes: Probably top-box versus top-two-box; primary report not read.

topic: How blends compare with conventional meat on liking
claim_a: Best blends matched or beat conventional (a 30 to 50 percent plant chicken mince beat 100 percent chicken; others within 0.5 points on a 7-point scale) (NOV-37, NOV-38)
claim_b: On average animal meat was liked by more tasters: 60 percent versus 37 percent for blends (NOV-40); or 81 percent versus 59 percent for blends and 44 percent for plant-based (NOV-38); animal protein ranks top, blends second, plant-based last
position_taken: Both are true: the best blends reach parity, the average blend does not. Design to the best-blend standard
notes: Averages versus best-in-class; the two average figures also differ between outlets, probably different scale cut-offs.

topic: Share of young Hanoi respondents aware of but not using novel alternative proteins (NOV-02)
claim_a: 84 percent, as stated in the text
position_taken: Use 70 percent, computed from the reported counts
notes: Possibly the 84 percent figure was carried over from RD-32, which reports 84 percent for its own sample.

claim_a: About 250,000 t per year and US$25 to 30 million exports (citing SGGP 2019, in NOV-78)
claim_b: About 24,780 t in 2021, forecast 26,620 t in 2026 (citing Reportlinker, in NOV-78)
position_taken: No position; both are secondary and cited in the same paper

claim_a: A cultivated meat product, 'exceptional in taste', sales to exceed prior years (company, NOV-10)
claim_b: With 97 percent plant ingredients it is effectively a plant-based product (Monash University professor, NOV-11)
position_taken: Treat it as a hybrid plant product with a small cultivated ingredient; its sales say little about demand for cultivated meat as such

claim_a: More than 5000 kg per week production and 35,000 litres capacity (company, NOV-16)
claim_b: About 25,000 dishes served in 16 months in Singapore and staff cuts of 30 percent in 2025 (NOV-14, NOV-16)
position_taken: Capacity is not demand; we rely on dishes served and restaurant counts
notes: Not a factual contradiction but a gap between supply claims and revealed sales.

topic: Stated share of Southeast Asians who would regularly eat plant-based meat if barriers were removed (Decoding Demand)
claim_a: About 63 percent, from 5 percent now (project document citing ECO-24)
claim_b: 'Three-quarters' would regularly consume; 50 percent often plus 15 percent always (GFI APAC press release, NOV-35)
position_taken: Report 'about two-thirds would often or always choose it', flag as a hypothetical stated measure
notes: Wording differs between GFI outputs; primary report not read.

topic: Openness of Vietnamese consumers to cultivated meat
claim_a: Vietnam is where the most open segment is concentrated (five-country study, NOV-01)
claim_b: Only about a quarter of young Vietnamese are 'optimists' about in vitro meat (NOV-03)
position_taken: Not a contradiction: Vietnam can be relatively open compared with Japan or Korea while most individuals are not optimists. Use both
notes: Neither study is tested or revealed.
